_comment: Preguntas ORIGINALES tipo NIE del capítulo 3.5. No son preguntas reales del examen. Comprueba con tu edición 2027.

questions.scenario: Which is the correct definition of aggravated burglary (s. 10 Theft Act 1968)?
options: Committing any burglary and at the time having with him a firearm/imitation firearm, weapon of offence or explosive
Burglary with two or more people

questions.scenario: Which memory aid lists the articles for aggravated burglary?
options: WIFE – weapon of offence, imitation firearm, firearm, explosive

questions.scenario: Burglars take cable ties to tie up the occupants of a house. Are the cable ties a weapon of offence?
options: Yes – a weapon of offence includes articles intended for incapacitating a person

questions.scenario: A burglar carries a screwdriver only to force windows and has no intention of using it on anyone. Is it a weapon of offence?
options: No – unless made/adapted for injury or intended for use to injure/incapacitate

questions.scenario: O'LEARY enters a house unarmed as a trespasser, picks up a knife in the kitchen and uses it to threaten the occupier while stealing. Is this aggravated burglary?
options: No, he wasn't armed on entry
Yes – for s. 9(1)(b) the article must be with him at the time of the stealing

questions.scenario: For a s. 9(1)(a) burglary, when must the defendant have the WIFE article with him?
A burglar carries a realistic plastic toy pistol. Which is correct?
options: Aggravated – an imitation firearm has the appearance of a firearm

questions.scenario: Does 'firearm' for s. 10 include an air pistol?
What is the maximum sentence for aggravated burglary?
How is aggravated burglary tried?
Three men commit a burglary; one secretly carries a knife. The others don't know. Are the others guilty of aggravated burglary?
options: Not unless they knew he had it (secondary liability)
Only if they also had knives
Only if the knife was used

questions.scenario: Must the burglar intend to USE a firearm he carries for it to be aggravated burglary?
options: No – having it with him is enough
questions.manualRef: Blackstone's 2027 · 3.5 · Firearm – no intent to use needed

questions.scenario: A burglar enters with a can of pepper spray intending to use it if disturbed. Which is correct?
options: It can be a weapon of offence (made for incapacitating / intended for such use)

questions.scenario: What is required before there can be an aggravated burglary?
A man enters a shop as a trespasser intending to steal, with a knife in his pocket that he forgot was there. Is this aggravated burglary?
options: Possibly not – 'has with him' generally requires knowledge (⚠ check)

questions.scenario: Which is NOT one of the WIFE articles?
options: Crowbar used only for breaking in

questions.scenario: Having entered a house as a trespasser without any weapon, a man finds a gun and takes it intending to sell it (he never uses it). Which is correct?
options: He may commit aggravated burglary: at the time of stealing he has a firearm with him
questions.manualRef: Blackstone's 2027 · 3.5 · Timing – stolen item as weapon

questions.scenario: An 'explosive' for s. 10 means…
options: an article manufactured for producing a practical effect by explosion, or intended for that purpose

questions.scenario: Is it necessary to show that the occupier saw the weapon?
Which offence should you consider first, before aggravated burglary, when a weapon is involved?
options: Whether there is a burglary (s. 9) at all
